picks.reasoning: Chovy and Ruler are the kind of individual players who decide a single game, and GEN's mid and bot lanes outclass what IG brings. The LCK-LPL gap is big enough that I'm not overthinking it, and IG's hype around IGRookie doesn't change my read.

This is a tempo game and GEN own the first 15 minutes: they take towers and dragons more often, and IG's early map control is shakier, so Chovy's lane gets to play fast while IG are still playing catch-up. Add the LCK's clear edge in this matchup and IG have to come back from behind, which they can do but rarely do cleanly.

Draft is where this one gets decided, and GEN's pool is deeper: Ryze, Syndra and Akali at mid, Lee Sin and Jarvan up top in the jungle, with Seraphine and Renata on support, all backed by a Chovy who is playing like a man who knows exactly what he wants to draft. IG has real champions, but they've shown more volatility in their own leads, and LCK's edge in this matchup is too big to ignore.

The region gap is the headline: LCK is clearly the stronger league, and GEN's 37-10 series record against IG's 18-25 is the cleanest sign of it. A single game is still volatile, so I'm leaning on the edge rather than calling it a lock.

GEN's room has learned to stay calm when the game turns, and that composure matters more than any single lane when it's one game with no second chance. IG has the spark, but a group that keeps needing comebacks to feel alive carries more nerves into a single elimination-style game, and the LCK's edge in this matchup sits underneath that.
